 Order
Aforesaid misc. appeal and civil revision have arisen out of common award dtd.10.01.2011 relating to same accident, therefore, are being decided by this common order.

2. This misc. appeal has been preferred by the appellants/non-applicants 1-2 (driver and owner)
challenging the award dtd.10.01.2011 passed by II Additional Member to Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni in MACC No.71/2010 whereby an amount of Rs.3,35,000/- has been awarded along with interest @ 6% p.a.
3.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Similarly, Civil Revision No.167/2011 has also been preferred by the appellants/non-applicants 1-2 (driver and owner) challenging the same award dtd.10.01.2011 passed by MACT in MACC No.72/2010 whereby an amount of Rs.3,000/- along with interest @ 6% p.a. has been awarded.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that vehicle Mahindra Pick- up bearing registration No. MP21-G-0467 was being driven by appellant 1- Rajesh Kumar who was possessing driving licence to drive Light Motor Vehicle (LMV), but there was no endorsement of commercial vehicle on it and on that ground, even though the vehicle was insured on the date of accident, the MACT has exonerated the non-applicant 3/Insurance Company-Ifco Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd.
from indemnifying the liability.

entities.text: Ifco Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
He submits that in the light of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors. (2017) 14 SCC 663,
the impugned award deserves to be modified because in the light of said decision, even if there was no endorsement on the licence to drive the commercial vehicle, insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability, because the driver was having LMV valid driving license.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors. (2017) 14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With these submissions he prays for setting aside/modifying the impugned award.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent 5/non-applicant 3/Insurance company does not dispute the aforesaid legal position.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

In the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under :
"46.
Section 10 of the Act requires a driver to hold a licence with respect to the class of vehicles and not with respect to the type of vehicles.
In one class of vehicles, there may be different kinds of vehicles.
If they fall in the same class of vehicles, no separate endorsement is required to drive such vehicles.
As light motor vehicle includes transport vehicle also, a holder of light motor vehicle licence can drive all the vehicles of the class including transport vehicles.
It was pre-amended position as well the post-amended position of Form 4 as amended on 28.3.2001.

Any other interpretation would be repugnant to the definition of "light motor vehicle" in section 2(21) and the provisions of section 10(2)(d), Rule 8 of the Rules of 1989, other provisions and also the forms which are in tune with the provisions.

Even otherwise the forms never intended to exclude transport vehicles from the category of `light motor vehicles' and for light motor vehicle, the validity period of such licence hold good and apply for the transport vehicle of such class also and the expression in Section 10(2)(e) of the Act `Transport Vehicle' would include medium goods vehicle,
medium passenger motor vehicle, heavy goods vehicle, heavy passenger motor vehicle which earlier found place in section 10(2)(e) to (h) and our conclusion is fortified by the syllabus and rules which we have discussed.

Thus we answer the questions which are referred to us thus:
(i) `Light motor vehicle' as defined in section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2(21) read with section 2(15)
and 2(48).
Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act No.54/1994.

2 (ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, `unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form.

(iii) The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act No.54/1994 w.e.f. 14.11.1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)(f),
heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in section 10(2)(h) with expression `transport vehicle' as substituted in section 10(2)(e)
related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.
It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of section 10(2)(d) and section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

(iv) The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect.
47.
In the light of aforesaid answer, let matters be placed for hearing on merits before the appropriate Bench."
8. In the present case it is undisputed fact on record that on the date of accident the appellant 1/non-applicant 1 was possessing driving licence to drive the LMV.

As such, in respect of the vehicle in question namely Mahindra Pick- up MP21-G-0468, although was being plied as a commercial vehicle, the insurance company was liable to indemnify the liability of owner of the vehicle.

9. In view of the aforesaid, impugned award deserves to be and is hereby modified and along with the appellants/non-applicants 1-2, the Insurance Company/non-applicant 3 is also held to be liable to pay the compensation awarded by MACT.
10. Resultantly, the appellants/non-applicant 1-2 as well as the Insurance Company shall be liable to pay the compensation, jointly and severally.
11. With the aforesaid, misc. appeal and civil revision are allowed and disposed off.
